match_winner.rederivation_notes: My chain from the KXATPMATCH/KXATPCHALLENGERMATCH/KXWTADOUBLES text ('wins ... after a ball has been played'; pre-start non-occurrence = fair price; postponement stays open two weeks): (1) participation gate and order-of-play/withdrawal timing, (2) court- and level-specific latent strength with uncertainty, (3) pair serve/return point probabilities (spw_A, spw_B), (4) day-of fatigue/injury modifiers, (5) point->game->set->match aggregation with a shared day shock and format (bo3/bo5/doubles match tiebreak), (6) mid-match retirement hazard whose settlement is NOT in the winner text. Required inputs: surface/pace-aware rating, adjusted serve/return, format, injury/withdrawal vintage, fatigue, rating uncertainty, level transfer, doubles pair strength. Comparison: the author's chain matches mine almost stage for stage and correctly flags the missing retirement sentence (the match-winner samples are under the 600-char cut so the absence is real, unlike the other variants). I verified hold(spw=.65)=.83. Differences: no in-play state, an unverifiable timestamped withdrawal-hazard claim, unverified primary data source, orphaned series.

findings.text: SOURCE_UNVERIFIED: every primary input here (surface_rating, opp_adjusted_serve_return, level_transfer_offset, doubles_pair_strength) lists 'Jeff Sackmann tennis_atp / tennis_wta match CSVs (GitHub)' as access 'free' with the note 'Tour-level, Challenger and ITF match rows with w_/l_ serve counts'. On 2026-11-07 raw.githubusercontent.com/JeffSackmann/tennis_atp (README.md and atp_matches_2024.csv) returned HTTP 404 while a control raw URL returned 200, and a third-party page (acesapi.com) reports both Sackmann repos 404 since 2026-10-14; not confirmed (could be proxy-specific). Separately, serve-count coverage of ITF/futures files and the existence of 'atp_matches_doubles' were not found in any source I could reach. Not listed in unresolved; 'free' label is unearned until the repo or a mirror is verified.
findings.resolution: DEFERRED_TO_UNRESOLVED:mw_sackmann_access

findings.text: ten.walkover_slot_hazard measurement promises 'report P(WO) at T-48h, T-12h, T-2h before scheduled start' from 'Sackmann score W/O rows'. A W/O score string carries no withdrawal timestamp, so the horizon-specific hazard cannot be estimated from that source; it needs own-captured entry/order-of-play snapshots. The tournament_winner_futures record itself declares this DATA_UNAVAILABLE ('tw_withdrawal_vintage: No free source archives entry list and draw states with timestamps'), so the two records contradict each other and match_winner has no matching unresolved entry. The input is also tagged role secondary/pregame_knowable partial while its estimation is impossible historically.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: ten.walkover_slot_hazard measurement rewritten as a day-level rate from W/O score rows only (no timestamps), horizon P(WO) moved to forward own-capture; added unresolved mw_wo_vintage (DATA_UNAVAILABLE) consistent with tournament_winner_futures tw_withdrawal_vintage; source label changed.

findings.text: Orphaned series: mw_misfiled_series lists KXWTABLETENNISMATCH ('Women's Table Tennis Match'), KXTENNISEXHIBITION and KXATPGWINNER as not sharing the winner mechanism, but no other TENNIS archetype record carries inputs for table tennis (different sport: rally model, best-of-5/7 games to 11) and exhibitions only get a context flag (ten.exhibition_format_effort). Nothing tells a downstream user these series have no input list.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: contract.series_mapping_issues added for KXATP/KXATPMEN/KXWTA/KXATPWTA/KXATPNATWINNER/KXATPTIEBREAK/KXATPGWINNER (named destination archetypes) and KXWTABLETENNISMATCH recorded as NEW_ARCHETYPE_NEEDED: table_tennis_match_winner; exhibitions remain here with only a context flag.

findings.text: ten.doubles_pair_strength measurement uses hand-set constants ('0.6*mean(doubles Elo ... n/(n+15)) + 0.25*pair Elo (zero if <5 shared matches) + 0.15*mean singles Elo scaled by 0.3') presented as the measurement; none is justified or marked as to-be-fitted, and the doubles source file is unverified (see MW-1). Doubles also use no-ad and a match tiebreak, which ten.format must code per tour; the record does not say which tour rule applies to Challenger doubles (KXATPCHALLENGERDOUBLES is TITLE_ONLY).
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: ten.doubles_pair_strength measurement now states its weights/constants are placeholders to be fitted, and added unresolved mw_doubles_format (CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS) for per-event doubles format incl. title-only Challenger doubles.

findings.text: Scope is pregame-only but undisclosed: KXATPMATCH/KXATPCHALLENGERMATCH markets are live during play (status 'active'/'finalized' samples), and there are no in-match state inputs (score, server, medical timeout) here; they exist only in game_winner_inplay. Also category_coverage lists pace_volume COVERED by ten.hold_break, which the author's own audit calls 'a transformation (spw to hold to match) rather than data' - nominal coverage.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: pre-match-only scope added to variants_and_edge_cases (live in-match state is not an input here); pace_volume changed from nominal COVERED by ten.hold_break to NOT_APPLICABLE with reason, since hold_break is a transformation.

findings.text: ten.player_speed_slope: CPI is 'event ace-rate/hold-rate index over the previous three editions' and beta_i is fit on the player's own last ~120 matches, which are part of that index (self-inclusion) and also reflect field composition; mw_speed_index_source discloses the contamination but not the self-inclusion leakage. Needs leave-player-out CPI.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: ten.player_speed_slope measurement now specifies a leave-player-out CPI (event index recomputed excluding the player's own matches, with baseline-adjusted residuals) removing self-inclusion; field-composition contamination still disclosed in mw_speed_index_source.

exact_set_score.rederivation_notes: My chain from KXATPEXACTMATCH/KXWTAEXACTMATCH ('wins ... by a set score of 2-1'; retirement clause 'all markets that can be unconditionally settled based on play already co...' cut at the evidence pack's 600-char limit, so the rest of the clause is genuinely unseen): format fixes the rung grid (4 bo3 / 6 bo5 rungs); P(winner) from pair strength; conditional split 2-0 vs 2-1 driven by set-level hold probabilities, tiebreak incidence, first-server order and between-set dependence (latent day shock plus fatigue/momentum); decider incidence; retirement truncation deciding which rungs settle. Required inputs: rating/pace, adjusted serve-return, format, within-match dependence, injury/fitness status, court pace, retirement timing/settlement. Comparison: the author's six stages match mine and the CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS handling is honest. Gaps: pre-match availability and environment are declared COVERED by outcome statistics rather than inputs, some dependence is assumed identifiable, and verdict labels are inconsistent.

findings.text: Coverage overstated: category_coverage marks availability_news COVERED by ['ten.retirement_timing_profile'] (a historical outcome statistic of when retirements occur) and environment COVERED by ['ten.match_length_expectation'] (which the author's own audit says is 'derived from hold probabilities, so not a free variable'). Neither is a pre-match availability or court input. An impaired-but-starting player shifts mass between 2-0 and 2-1, and court pace moves hold and tiebreak incidence, yet ten.fitness/ten.withdrawal_signals and ten.court_cond/ten.venue_speed_history/ten.player_speed_slope (all used in match_winner/total_games) are not attached. These should be GAP or attached; the required input list is incomplete.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: availability_news now COVERED by ten.fitness, ten.withdrawal_signals (+ retirement_timing_profile as outcome statistic) and environment by ten.court_cond, ten.venue_speed_history; attached to stages s2/s5/s6 and to required_data feeds so the court-pace and impaired-starter channels are in the input list.

findings.text: SOURCE_UNVERIFIED: new inputs straight_set_share_curve and retirement_timing_profile and the whole calibration chain rely on 'Sackmann CSVs (score strings)' and 'tennis_slam_pointbypoint' (Slams only, 'limited' per the author). Sackmann raw URLs returned 404 from this environment on 2026-11-07 (third-party report: repos 404 since 2026-10-14; unconfirmed) and ten.set_first_server_sequence needs toss data the author concedes has no archive (es_toss_info). The between-set dependence the author calls the key parameter is, by es_dependence_estimation, identified only from Slam point data - so the primary input within_match_dependence has no verified source at all.
findings.resolution: DEFERRED_TO_UNRESOLVED:es_sackmann_access

findings.text: Audit verdicts inconsistent: ten.serve_return is 'DUPLICATE_OF:ten.surface_rating' here, but a rating (Elo) and raw point-win rates are different quantities (in match_winner/game_winner it is DUPLICATE_OF opp_adjusted_serve_return, in totals/sweep DUPLICATE_OF hold_break). ten.match_length_expectation is KEEP_SECONDARY here, DUPLICATE_OF games_per_set_distribution in total_games_and_sets, and KEEP_PRIMARY in aces. ten.set_dist is KEEP_PRIMARY although the author states it is 'an output of the model rather than a raw input'.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: serve_return verdict changed from DUPLICATE_OF surface_rating to KEEP_SECONDARY (raw rates are not a rating), set_dist downgraded to KEEP_CONTEXT as a model output, and match_length_expectation kept KEEP_SECONDARY with a cross-record consistency note (the duplicate in total_games_and_sets is corrected there).

findings.text: Interaction ['ten.fatigue','ten.decider_record'] (threshold) and nonlinearity on ten.tiebreak rest on inputs the author's own audit rates WEAK ('tiny samples and mostly noise'; 'regress heavily to serve strength'). An interaction between a weak input and a small-effect modifier is not evidence of a real interaction; either drop or re-base on straight_set_share_curve / set_number_calibration.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: dropped the fatigue x decider_record interaction and the weak ten.tiebreak nonlinearity; replaced by a straight_set_share_curve x match_length_expectation conditional interaction and a saturating-in-edge nonlinearity on straight_set_share_curve, both with tests.

game_winner_inplay.rederivation_notes: No live series and no rules text for this key. My chain: a game is a race to 4 points (win by 2); the outcome is a closed-form function of the server's per-point win probability and the current point score; the real work is the running posterior of that probability (pregame pair prior, within-match first-serve/ace/DF drift, medical timeouts, wind/ball age/side), plus deuce-leverage non-linearity and who serves. Settlement hazards: tiebreak counted as a game or not, interrupted game at retirement/suspension, point penalties. I recomputed the game-hold function (spw .60/.65/.70 -> .736/.830/.901), matching the author's .74/.90. Comparison: the author's stages s1-s5 match my chain closely; the outcome-irrelevant execution layer (feed latency, trade tape) is mixed into the outcome input list, and real game-winner series are filed in other archetypes so this record's contract basis is empty.

findings.text: Market-derived/execution items inside the outcome chain: stage s6 'Settlement feed and execution timing' lists ['ten.score_feed_latency','m.trade_tape'], interaction ['ten.score_feed_latency','m.trade_tape'] is registered as a mechanism interaction, and ten.score_feed_latency is KEEP_PRIMARY. Latency changes when a trader can act, not P(player wins the game); m.trade_tape is audited BENCHMARK_ONLY ('market data ... not a determinant of the game outcome') yet is used as a stage input, interaction input and feeds_inputs target. Per the brief, price-derived values are benchmarks, not inputs. Move latency/tape to a separate execution-evidence section and demote to context.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: removed ten.score_feed_latency and m.trade_tape from stage inputs and the latency x tape interaction; stage s6 rebuilt around settlement/interrupted-game rules, latency downgraded to KEEP_CONTEXT execution evidence, tape feed moved out of the outcome inputs, new settlement register dataset added.

findings.text: Series mis-mapping not resolved: the ledger holds KXATPGWINNER ('ATP Game Winner', filed under match_winner) and KXATPS1GWINNER/S3/S4/S5 ('ATP set N game winner', filed under set_winner_and_any_set) - five TITLE_ONLY live series that are plausibly this archetype's contracts - yet this record says NO_LIVE_SERIES and set_winner_and_any_set speculates they 'might refer to a game within a set'. Neither record owns them; the identity of the game (parity, hold vs break), tiebreak handling and set indexing are unknown to both. rules_verification should be TITLE_ONLY-like, and the ledger/archetype assignment should be fixed before the inputs here are relied on.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: contract.series_mapping_issues lists KXATPGWINNER and KXATPS1/3/4/5GWINNER as plausible game_winner_inplay series (currently filed elsewhere); record claims made explicitly conditional; game identity itself remains open in gw_no_rules. Ledger refiling is outside this record.

findings.text: ten.ball_change_cycle: stage s4 states as fact that 'new balls are introduced after the first seven games and then every nine' and the measurement codes '(total games played - 7) mod 9 for events with the 7/9 schedule', while gw_ball_effect_unverified says the schedule and effect are unverified. Ball-change conventions differ by event (the numbers count the warm-up as games at some events) so the formula is event-dependent and needs a per-event register, which is not in required_data.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: stage s4 no longer states the 7/9 schedule as fact, ten.ball_change_cycle measurement now uses a per-event schedule register (warm-up counting, differing intervals) and a Per-event ball-change schedule register dataset was added to required_data.

findings.text: SOURCE_UNVERIFIED: calibration of the prior strength k and ball/side effects depends on 'Jeff Sackmann tennis_slam_pointbypoint' and the Match Charting Project, both under the Sackmann account that returned 404 from this environment on 2026-11-07 (unconfirmed); the pair-prior dataset also leans on Sackmann CSVs. No fallback is stated beyond paid vendors with 'field list not verified'.
findings.resolution: DEFERRED_TO_UNRESOLVED:gw_sackmann_access

nationality_and_team_futures.rederivation_notes: No live series here, but KXATPNATWINNER ('If an American woman wins the women's singles title ... nationalities reflect those designated by the Governing League') and KXATPNATSTAGE ('If 1+ Americans reach the Final', greater_or_equal 1) are in the evidence under other archetypes. My chain: roster of players the league designates to the nation -> individual title/stage probabilities from a path simulation -> bracket dependence (compatriots in one half cannot both reach the Final; a meeting removes one with certainty) -> union/threshold aggregation (final stage count 0-2) -> designation/neutral edge cases; team events (Davis Cup etc.) would be rubber models with lineup and host-surface effects, but no team series is live. Required inputs: designation register, pre-draw field/withdrawal, path simulation marginals, collision matrix, bracket covariance. The author's chain matches; differences: roles and effort for team contracts without any live series, and the real nationality contracts not used as verified evidence.

findings.text: Mis-mapping weakens verification: the two verifiable contracts that define this archetype (KXATPNATWINNER filed under match_winner; KXATPNATSTAGE/KXWTANATSTAGE under tournament_winner_futures) carry rules text, but this record is NO_LIVE_SERIES with empty rules_evidence, so its settlement claims ('a union over all compatriots', 'at most two players at the Final') remain 'inferred' even though the text exists elsewhere. Meanwhile KXATPNATSTAGE is also analysed in tournament_winner_futures, so the union/count mechanism is split across three records with no single owner.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: settlement_definition and variants now cite the live KXATPNATWINNER/KXATPNATSTAGE rules text read from the evidence pack, state this record owns the union/count mechanism, and contract.series_mapping_issues lists KXATPNATWINNER, KXATPNATSTAGE, KXWTANATSTAGE; rules_verification stays NO_LIVE_SERIES because the ledger files none under this archetype.

findings.text: Effort and roles misallocated to unlisted contracts: of six new inputs, four (team_tie_lineup_distribution role primary, host_surface_selection, team_group_tiebreak_rules, plus ten.team_event_structure kept KEEP_PRIMARY) serve Davis Cup/BJK/United Cup/Laver Cup contracts that nt_no_live_rules says were not found live, while the only live evidenced mechanisms (nationality winner, stage count) rest on collision matrix and designation register. Primary roles for team inputs are unsupported by any contract; they should be context/conditional until a team series is listed.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: team inputs (lineup distribution, host surface, group tiebreak rules) downgraded from primary/secondary to context and ten.team_event_structure audited KEEP_CONTEXT; stages s5/s6 marked conditional; new unresolved nt_team_roles_conditional records that no team series is listed.

findings.text: ten.home_slam_depth_prior and ten.nationality_field_strength interaction ('saturating') and the 0.3 shrinkage weight toward the model are hand-set; home_slam_depth_prior is a frequency of past home progress and so partly re-encodes the model output it is meant to shrink toward. Interaction ['ten.home_slam_depth_prior','ten.nationality_field_strength'] is an aggregation identity (union saturation), not an interaction between two measurable inputs.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: home_slam_depth_prior 0.3 weight marked a placeholder and the input restricted to out-of-sample calibration use; the aggregation-identity interaction was replaced by a fitness x compatriot_collision_matrix conditional interaction with a test.

findings.text: Nationality designation: the author cites 'designated by the Governing League' but proposes ATP/WTA player profiles and Wikipedia as sources and does not state which one the contract would follow when ATP and WTA flags differ from the draw sheet; also ten.nationality_designation_status measurement includes 'probability designation changes before settlement' without a data source for estimating it.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: designation measurement now names the draw-sheet flag as primary with profile as check, treats designation change as a scenario flag rather than an invented hazard, and unresolved nt_designation_source records the ambiguity over which source the contract follows.

player_aces_and_double_faults.rederivation_notes: No live series or rules for this key. My chain: count = per-point rate x exposure. Exposure = service points = service games x points per game + tiebreak serve points, endogenous to match length (straight-set wins are short); rate = P(first serve in) x P(ace | in) + second-serve ace rate, depending on server pace/height, returner reach/position, court speed/altitude/ball, wind, line-calling regime; day-level overdispersion (negative binomial); double faults tied to second-serve risk under pressure; settlement: official stat vs vendor feed, retirement truncation of the count, tiebreak/match-tiebreak points. Required inputs: server rate, returner adjustment, service-point scenario mixture, conditions, count distribution, settlement source, retirement hazard/truncation, injury state. Comparison: the author's stages s1-s5 are good and the exposure-rate negative correlation is a real catch. Missing: retirement/availability inputs in the truncation stage and source viability.

findings.text: Truncation stage has no truncation input: s6 'Counting rule and truncation' says 'a retirement stops the count at that moment' and variants say over-rungs may settle early, but its input_ids are ['ten.ace_settlement_source','ten.first_serve_speed_trend'] only; no retirement-hazard, retirement-timing or settlement-rule input is attached (those exist in the sibling records: ten.retirement_timing_profile, ten.retirement_games_completed_profile, ten.retirement_settlement_rules). availability_news is GAP although ten.fitness and ten.withdrawal_signals exist in the catalog and the gap text only argues serve-specific injury info is missing. The required input list omits the retirement/availability block that changes the counted exposure.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: retirement block attached: retirement_settlement_rules, retirement_base_rate and fitness added to stage s6, retirement_base_rate to s1, availability_news now COVERED by fitness/withdrawal_signals/retirement_base_rate, scenario mixture measurement truncates exposure at retirement, plus an availability/retirement dataset; serve-specific injury stays in ac_injury_gap.

findings.text: SOURCE_UNVERIFIED: the primary rate inputs (ace_opp_adjusted, second_serve_risk_policy, service_points_scenario_mixture, player aces/DF counts) have 'Jeff Sackmann tennis_atp / tennis_wta match CSVs (GitHub)' as the sole free source ('w_/l_ serve counts (ace, df, svpt'). Sackmann raw URLs returned 404 from this environment on 2026-11-07 (third-party report: 404 since 2026-10-14; unconfirmed), and ITF/futures serve-count coverage is unverified. Direction and speed inputs depend on MatchChartingProject (same account, 'coverage skews to famous players') or Hawk-Eye feeds the author labels unavailable_public, so serve_direction_mix_vs_returner and first_serve_speed_trend are effectively unsourced; only partially disclosed in ac_injury_gap.
findings.resolution: DEFERRED_TO_UNRESOLVED:ac_sackmann_access

findings.text: ten.aces_df is marked DUPLICATE_OF:ten.ace_opp_adjusted, but aces_df covers aces and double faults while ace_opp_adjusted is aces only; double-fault markets then depend solely on second_serve_risk_policy (itself a new, 'partial' measurable input) and double_fault_pressure (also DUPLICATE). The DF side of the archetype has no KEEP-level existing input.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: ten.aces_df re-audited from DUPLICATE_OF ace_opp_adjusted to KEEP_SECONDARY because it is the only existing raw double-fault-rate and serve-speed ingredient; the DF side is paired with second_serve_risk_policy.

findings.text: Interaction ['ten.serve_direction_mix_vs_returner','ten.return_style_rally'] is described as 'the product of the server's mass and the returner's miss rate over directions defines the ace rate' - an accounting identity, not an interaction to test; and the audit concedes return_style_rally is a 'coarse proxy' for the returner reach/position the mechanism says is decisive. Also unsourced magnitudes ('ace|in about 0.05-0.30', 'variance 1.5-3 times the mean') are stated as facts in stage distributions.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: identity-style direction x return-style interaction replaced by a first_serve_speed_trend x second_serve_risk_policy conditional regime interaction with a test; unsourced magnitudes in stage distributions relabelled illustrative / to be estimated.

findings.text: Whether any aces/DF series exists is unknown (NO_LIVE_SERIES); the stage and input roles (many primary) should be marked conditional on listing, and per-player versus match-total markets (a sum of two dependent counts) have no input for the cross-player correlation beyond a prose variant.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: variants now state roles and stages are conditional on a series being listed (none is), and unresolved ac_pair_correlation added for the cross-player count correlation needed by match-total markets.

retirement_walkover_participation.rederivation_notes: Three contracts, three mechanisms. KXATPCOMPETE ('competes in the 2026 US Open men's singles tournament'): entry -> draw -> not withdrawn before first ball; 'competes' undefined. KXATPRETURN ('competes in an ATP Match after May 19, 2026 and before September 1, 2026', US Open counts): layoff recovery x eligible events x entry decision x withdrawal hazard. KXATPRETIRE ('announces his retirement ... before 2027', 'effective immediately or prior to 2027'): age/career-stage hazard with injury, with announcement defined by a player/team statement. My required inputs: injury/layoff state and recovery curve, entry eligibility (rank cutoff, protected ranking, wildcards), incentives, withdrawal timeline vintage, retirement-announcement hazard, and an explicit definition of what counts as an ATP match/competing. Comparison: the author's stages match; unflagged gap is the scope of 'ATP Match' and some verification/quote overreach.

findings.text: Undisclosed contract gap: KXATPRETURN settles on 'competes in an ATP Match' and the secondary note says 'The US Open Tennis Championships is part of the ATP Tour and therefore would count as an ATP Match' - implying scope is a deliberate boundary. The record's variants discuss walkovers, windows and retirement scope but never ask whether Challenger, Davis Cup/Laver Cup, exhibitions, Olympics or ATP Cup-style team events count as an 'ATP Match'; none appears in unresolved. This changes the eligible-event set in ten.eligible_event_calendar (described only as 'ATP/WTA official calendar ... category') and therefore the P(enter) product for any returning player.
findings.resolution: DEFERRED_TO_UNRESOLVED:rp_atp_match_scope

findings.text: Quote overreach: the 'establishes' for KXATPRETIRE ('The retirement must be intended to be effective immediately or prior to 2027') says 'a farewell season does not count'. A farewell season ending before 2027 would satisfy that note; only a retirement effective in 2027 or later fails. The variant bullet is correct ('retire at the end of 2027'), the evidence annotation is not.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: KXATPRETIRE rules_evidence 'establishes' rewritten: a farewell season ending before 2027 satisfies the note; only a retirement effective in 2027 or later fails it, matching the quoted sentence and the variant bullet.

findings.text: rules_verification is VERIFIED_FROM_RULES_TEXT although the record's own unresolved items state that 'competes' is undefined (walkover after draw, first-game retirement), the source of truth is unnamed and the announcement scope is not visible; PARTIALLY_VERIFIED is the honest label.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: rules_verification changed from VERIFIED_FROM_RULES_TEXT to PARTIALLY_VERIFIED, with a variant noting undefined 'competes', unnamed source of truth and unknown announcement channel.

findings.text: Irrelevant inputs inflate coverage: environment is COVERED by ['ten.heat_humidity','ten.suspension_postponement_risk'] which the author audits WEAK and IRRELEVANT, and both remain in the 'Tournament calendar and rules' feeds_inputs; ten.fitness is DUPLICATE_OF injury_comeback yet still in stage s1 inputs; m.settlement_truth/m.lifecycle (KEEP_CONTEXT, 'do not drive outcomes') sit in stage s6 inputs. Environment should be NOT_APPLICABLE and these removed.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: environment set NOT_APPLICABLE with reason; heat_humidity and suspension_postponement_risk removed from coverage and feeds, ten.fitness removed from stage s1 (duplicate of injury_comeback), m.settlement_truth/m.lifecycle removed from stage s6 and feeds.

findings.text: Roles are archetype-wide but each input serves one contract: retirement_announcement_hazard (primary) is irrelevant to COMPETE/RETURN, and layoff_survival_curve, withdrawal_hazard_timeline (primary) are irrelevant to RETIRE. rp_ledger_filing admits the three 'share only a topic'; inputs should carry a per-series applicability tag. Also retirement_announcement_hazard rests on 'Wikipedia retirement lists' of players with 8+ year careers - survivorship toward players who announced, with no source for announcement dates.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: series_applicability map added to the record, applies_to tags and why-prefixes put on retirement_announcement_hazard (KXATPRETIRE only), layoff_survival_curve and withdrawal_hazard_timeline (not RETIRE); survivorship fix added to the hazard measurement and unresolved rp_announcement_dates records the date-source gap.

season_ranking_and_majors.rederivation_notes: From KXATP1RANK/KXATPT5RANK/KXWTA1RANK ('#1 ranked on the PIF ATP singles rankings on Dec 31, 2026 at 12:00 PM ET'; 'most recently published PIF ATP Rankings'), KXATPGRANDSLAM/KXWTAGRANDSLAM ('wins a tennis major ... after Issuance and before Dec 31, 2027') and KXATPNOVAK25 ('25th career major', singles only). My chain: rank = 52-week rolling points: current points - dropping points + earned in remaining events (bounded arithmetic with threshold behaviour); participation of leaders in remaining events; indoor-hard strength; publication calendar (Dec 31, 2026 is a Thursday, so the last Monday list applies); majors = union of four dependent lotteries (health, entry, bo5 strength, draw) with concentration; cumulative contract adds career-count state and longevity. I checked the ATP Finals points (200/400/500 -> 1500 undefeated). Comparison: the author's chain is close; differences: finals-qualification contracts left to another archetype, a wrong remaining-events claim, and an overstated verification label.

findings.text: Archetype/series mis-mapping: the archetype target is 'Season-end ranking, number of majors, or qualification for a season finals', but KXATPFINALSQUAL/KXWTAFINALSQUAL ('Will Player Qualify for ATP Finals?') are filed in tournament_winner_futures, where the new primary input ten.finals_cutoff_race (race points, points available, 8th-place cutoff, alternates) is essentially the same mechanism as this record's ten.remaining_race_arithmetic under a different id. This record never mentions finals qualification at all (no cutoff, alternates or doubles-team rules), so one mechanism has two near-duplicate inputs split across two records and neither is complete.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: Finals-qualification series recorded as incoming in contract.series_mapping_issues (and as outgoing in tournament_winner_futures); the duplicate ten.finals_cutoff_race was removed and both records now share one ten.remaining_race_arithmetic definition extended with the 8th-place cutoff and alternates; unresolved sr_finals_qual_contracts added.

findings.text: Factual slip in the summary: 'the remaining maximum swing' is attributed partly to 'team events' ('the final Masters, the Finals, team events'). Davis Cup/BJK Cup/Laver Cup finals do not award ATP/WTA ranking points, so they matter only via participation/withdrawal from point-bearing events (ten.motivation), not as a points swing; remaining_race_arithmetic correctly lists points tables but the narrative implies otherwise.

set_and_game_spreads.rederivation_notes: From KXATPGSPREAD ('game differential in favor of X across the full match is above 1.5 games'; strike 1.5; retirement clause cut at 600 chars): D = games_A - games_B summed over all sets. Mechanism: per-game increment mean is (hold_A - hold_B) (an alternating-serve pair of games contributes 2*(hA-hB)), so E[D] = E[number of games played] x (hA-hB), NOT a fixed 12 per set; per-set margin is bounded by set-ending rules (6-0..6-4 = 6..2, 7-5 = 2, 7-6 = 1); number of sets is endogenous (straight-set wins stop early); winner-and-margin joint event (D can be negative for the match winner, e.g. 7-6 0-6 7-6); serial/day-shock dependence widens D; retirement truncation. Required inputs: adjusted serve/return -> holds, format and deciding-set rule, tiebreak incidence, win probability, margin PMF, court pace, retirement margin state. Comparison: stage structure matches; the quantitative spec of the primary new input is wrong and environment/source gaps are self-inflicted.

findings.text: Primary new input mis-specified: ten.hold_gap_expected_margin measurement is 'For each set compute E[D_set] = G*(h_A - h_B) with G=12'. The mean margin per game is (h_A - h_B), so the multiplier must be the expected number of games actually played in the set (about 9-10 for tour sets, since sets end at 6-x/7-5 and 7-6 count 13), not a fixed 12. With G=12 the expected margin is overstated by roughly a fifth (e.g. hA=.85, hB=.75: 1.2 vs about 0.95 games per set). The summary's '12 times the hold-rate gap' is only valid 'over a 12-game window'. As defined the input would be biased and its 'standard deviation' wrong; it is tagged primary.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: ten.hold_gap_expected_margin now uses E[N_set] (about 10 games, from a DP) instead of G=12; verified by DP that h_A=0.85, h_B=0.75 gives about 1.03 not 1.20 (overstated about 17%); the summary's '12 times' wording corrected to apply only over a fixed 12-game window.

findings.text: Self-inflicted environment GAP: category_coverage environment = GAP and sp_court_pace is typed DATA_UNAVAILABLE ('no public per-event court-pace index was verified'), yet the sibling total_games_and_sets record attaches ten.venue_speed_history (event hold history) to the same mechanism (hold level) and match_winner has ten.court_cond/ten.player_speed_slope. Court pace shifts both holds and tiebreak mass, i.e. the variance and cap of D. Inputs that exist in the catalog should be attached; the 'unavailable' typing contradicts the other records. situational_schedule_motivation is covered only by ten.fatigue, which the author rates WEAK.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: environment moved from GAP to COVERED by ten.venue_speed_history and ten.court_cond (same inputs as the totals record), workload_minutes attached for schedule/fatigue, and sp_court_pace re-typed SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for the missing pace index only.

Also the set-spread series KXATPSSPREAD, which matches this archetype's target 'Game or set differential', is 'analysed' in set_winner_and_any_set, so no set-differential input list lives here.

set_sweep_and_tiebreak_events.rederivation_notes: No live series assigned; the nearest titles are KXATPTIEBREAK ('Tiebreak to occur in Match', filed under match_winner) and KXATPSETSWEEP ('Winner without dropping a set', filed under set_winner_and_any_set), both TITLE_ONLY. My chain: tiebreak occurs iff some set reaches 6-6 (rare under ~0.75 holds, convex in holds), union over sets played, with set count itself random and correlated; dependent across sets through day shock; sweep = winner takes every set (match level) or a tournament-level run without dropping a set (a very different path product over rounds). Required inputs: both hold probabilities with uncertainty (Jensen correction), deciding-set rule and format, event tiebreak base rates, within-match dependence, serve profile, injury status; for a tournament-level sweep also draw path, round-by-round win and straight-set probabilities. I recomputed P(6-6) at equal holds 0.75/0.80/0.85/0.90 = 0.181/0.217/0.276/0.379, matching the author. Comparison: mechanics correct; the tournament-level sweep reading has no inputs here and one stated mechanism claim is wrong.

findings.text: Missing inputs for the more likely sweep reading: 'Winner without dropping a set' (KXATPSETSWEEP) reads most naturally as a tournament-winner contract; ss_no_live_series/sw_sweep_definition list the tournament-level reading as possible, but stage s5 and all new inputs here model only the match-level straight-set event. ten.tournament_set_drop_path (the draw/round product) exists only in set_winner_and_any_set as a 'context' input assigned to a retirement stage, and no draw/seeding/round-by-round data appear in this record's required_data. If the tournament reading holds, the required input list here is wrong.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: tournament-reading inputs added (ten.tournament_set_drop_path moved here, ten.draw, shared set_count_distribution_by_edge) with a draw/round dataset, both sweep readings carried side by side, and unresolved ss_sweep_scope records that the scope is unsettled for the title-only series.

findings.text: Wrong necessary condition: stage s1 says 'The tiebreak requires holds in at least ten of the first twelve games and a specific split'. A set reaches 6-6 whenever each player wins six of the first twelve games without either leading by two at 6-x; four or more breaks (alternating breaks) still produce 6-6. Ten holds is the modal path, not a requirement; the DP in ten.hold_rate_uncertainty_propagation handles it correctly, so only the stage text is wrong.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: stage s1 text corrected: a tiebreak needs the set to reach 6-6 (each player six of the first twelve games), ten holds being only the modal path; I verified the stated 6-6 probabilities (0.18/0.22/0.28/0.38 at holds 0.75-0.90) by DP.

set_winner_and_any_set.rederivation_notes: From KXATPSETWINNER/KXWTASETWINNER ('wins set 2'), KXATPTOTALSETS ('above 4.5 sets are played'), KXATPSSPREAD ('wins by over 1.5 sets'); retirement clause cut at 600 chars; ANYSET, S1-S5GWINNER, SETSWEEP are TITLE_ONLY. My chain: a set is a race to six with tiebreak at 6-6 from the two hold probabilities and first server; set k exists only after prior sets (cascade: bo3 set 3 only at 1-1); set-index effects (first set, deciding set) and between-set dependence; aggregation to the settled quantity (marginal of one named set / number of sets / signed set margin); unplayed or interrupted set settlement. Required inputs: adjusted serve/return and holds, tiebreak reach, set-index calibration, set-count distribution by edge, within-match dependence, fatigue, injury/withdrawal, court pace, format. Comparison: the author's s1-s5 match and the unplayed-set ambiguity is a real catch; gaps: environment left as GAP, magnitudes contradict a sibling record, and filing/stage mismatches.

total_games_and_sets.rederivation_notes: From KXATPGAMETOTAL/KXATPGTOTAL/KXWTAGTOTAL ('the number of completed games in the full match is above 32.5/28.5/26.5'; half-point strikes, no push; retirement clause cut at 600 chars). My chain: total = sum over sets of games per set; set count (2-3 bo3, 3-5 bo5) set by closeness AND by between-set dependence (a shared day shock raises both straight-set and decider mass); games per set from the two holds (6-0 .. 7-6 = 6..13, tiebreak = 13), with tiebreak mass convex in hold; deciding-set rule (tiebreak at 6-6 vs advantage set) sets the right tail; environment shifts both holds together; retirement truncates the count ('completed' excludes an interrupted game) so over-rungs can settle early but unders cannot. Required inputs: adjusted holds, set-count distribution with dependence, format/deciding rule, tiebreak reach, court pace, retirement profile/settlement. Comparison: the author's stages align; the omission is the dependence input, and sets markets are not covered here.

findings.text: Between-set dependence omitted: stage s2 calls set count 'the largest single lever on the total', and interaction 1 says close matches 'co-move' with long sets, but no input in this record (existing, audited or new) measures between-set/day-shock dependence - ten.within_match_dependence, ten.set_count_distribution_by_edge and ten.set_number_calibration live only in the set_winner/exact_set records. s2 inputs are ['ten.surface_rating','ten.match_length_expectation','ten.games_per_set_distribution'] and match_length_expectation is marked DUPLICATE. Dependence widens the total's variance and decider mass, i.e. it changes P(total>k) on every rung; the required input list is missing it.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: ten.within_match_dependence and the shared ten.set_count_distribution_by_edge added to stage s2, coverage, feeds and a new joint-distribution interaction, so between-set dependence and decider mass now enter every over-rung and total-sets rung.

findings.text: Settlement conventions asserted from convention, not text: 'a tiebreak set contributing 13 games (7-6)' and 'a deciding-set 10-point tiebreak at 6-6 contributes 13 games' are stated as facts; the rule says only 'completed games in the full match'. Only the doubles/exhibition match-tiebreak is flagged (tg_match_tiebreak); the ordinary 7-point and Slam deciding tiebreak counting is not.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: tiebreak-counts-as-one-game and deciding-set conventions rewritten as assumptions not in the sampled text in settlement_definition and the variants; tg_match_tiebreak widened to cover the ordinary 7-point and Slam deciding tiebreak counting.

findings.text: Duplicate bookkeeping: ten.final_set_rule is DUPLICATE_OF:ten.decider_format_tail yet still appears in interactions, a nonlinearity and feeds_inputs; ten.match_length_expectation is DUPLICATE here but KEEP elsewhere; m.ladder_structure (market structure) and m.strike_hit_rates (BENCHMARK_ONLY, a market-calibration table) are listed in the 'Event register with format and condition' feeds_inputs although neither is an outcome determinant. KXATPTOTALSETS is analysed in set_winner_and_any_set, so total sets has no set-count input here.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: final_set_rule replaced by its kept duplicate ten.decider_format_tail across stages, interactions, nonlinearities and feeds; match_length_expectation changed to KEEP_SECONDARY; m.ladder_structure and m.strike_hit_rates removed from feeds and coverage; total-sets set-count input now attached here.

The ITF rating classifies surface products/tested courts, not necessarily each event's courts. Sackmann is the sole free source for games_per_set_distribution and player_games_residual and returned 404 from this environment on 2026-11-07 (unconfirmed; third-party report since 2026-10-14).

tournament_winner_futures.rederivation_notes: From KXATPADVANCE/KXWTAADVANCE ('qualifies for the Final ... if they qualify but do not end up competing, the market will still resolve to Yes'), KXATPNATSTAGE ('1+ Americans reach the Final'); outright, FINALS, NEXTGEN, FINALSQUAL series TITLE_ONLY. My chain: field formation (entry, pre- and post-draw withdrawals, alternates) -> draw/seeding structure (random subject to seeding; pre-draw averaging vs post-draw conditional path) -> match win probabilities with uncertainty on the event's court -> path dependence (fatigue, in-event form, injury) -> within-draw dependence (same-half exclusivity, shared upset shocks) -> round-robin structure for Finals/Next Gen (group tie-breaks) -> stage-contract settlement (reaching the final slot pays even on walkover) and season-race cutoff logic for Finals qualification contracts. Required inputs: ratings with uncertainty, pace, draw, field/withdrawal vintage, fatigue/in-event update, round-robin rules, race arithmetic. Comparison: the author's chain matches; issues are mapping duplication, audit direction and format modelling.

findings.text: Finals-qualification contracts (KXATPFINALSQUAL, KXWTAFINALSQUAL, both TITLE_ONLY) are filed here though season_ranking_and_majors' target is 'qualification for a season finals'. ten.finals_cutoff_race (primary: race points, remaining events, 8th-place cutoff, alternates, 'participation hazard') duplicates season_ranking's ten.remaining_race_arithmetic under another id, and neither record owns the 8th-place cutoff, alternates rule and doubles-team qualification. The mechanism is not tournament-path at all (no draw); the required input set for these series is split and duplicated.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: KXATPFINALSQUAL/KXWTAFINALSQUAL mapped to season_ranking_and_majors in contract.series_mapping_issues; ten.finals_cutoff_race deleted and replaced by the single shared ten.remaining_race_arithmetic definition (identical in both records) in stages, coverage, interactions, nonlinearities and feeds.

Also ten.round_context is WEAK but listed in stage s2.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: audit reversed so ten.draw (the measured bracket) is KEEP_PRIMARY and path_difficulty_sim/bracket_correlation are KEEP_CONTEXT model outputs; round_context removed from stage s2 and coverage; the bracket_correlation x race interaction rebuilt on ten.draw.

combo_tournament_winners.rederivation_notes: No live series, no rules text. The only candidate is KXATPWTA 'Men and Women Tournament Winners' (TITLE_ONLY, filed under match_winner). The title does not establish a combination: it could be a single-event market listing both men's and women's champions, or a multi-leg joint contract. My chain, conditional on a joint contract being real: leg definitions and mutual exclusivity (same event, different players), marginals from path simulations, dependence only where legs share a player (strength, health persistence, calendar load) or share conditions (weather, cross-tour), and conditional collapse as legs resolve. Required inputs: rules identification of legs (the decisive unknown), per-leg marginals, entry/withdrawal state, and for same-player combos cross-surface covariance and carryover. Comparison: the author's mathematics is sound but built entirely on guesses about the contract structure, and labels guesses as primary inputs.

findings.text: Primary inputs justified by an invented contract: cross_surface_rating_covariance (role primary), slam_to_slam_carryover and health_persistence_between_events exist only for the 'same player wins two named tournaments' reading, which nothing in the single TITLE_ONLY title 'Men and Women Tournament Winners' supports (a men's+women's title would involve different players, where these inputs are irrelevant). The record's own settlement text says 'every statement here is inferred'. Roles should be conditional on identifying the legs, and the first required deliverable (m.rules_text / leg identification) should be primary; currently the leg-structure uncertainty does not change the input roles.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: cross_surface_rating_covariance, slam_to_slam_carryover and health_persistence changed from primary/secondary to context with applies_to 'same-player legs' and a why-prefix; leg identification (ten.leg_resolution_state, m.rules_text) made primary and stage s1 states it is required first.

findings.text: Non-interactions and circularity: interaction ['ten.bracket_correlation','ten.leg_resolution_state'] ('mutually exclusive ... correlation is negative and exactly known') is a structural identity, not an interaction between measurable inputs; ['ten.fitness','ten.joint_event_correlation'] uses the contract's own outcome-defined quantity (the author audits joint_event_correlation as 'defined only as an outcome' yet KEEP_PRIMARY) as an input.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: the bracket_correlation x leg_resolution_state identity replaced by a covariance x pre_draw_field interaction; joint_event_correlation (outcome-defined) re-audited KEEP_CONTEXT and removed from stages, coverage and feeds, and its interaction/nonlinearity re-based on health_persistence.

The leg_resolution_state rationale mentions 'the live price path', mixing price dynamics into an input definition.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: m.external_lines and ten.motivation removed from the legs/resolution dataset feeds and the price-path wording removed from leg_resolution_state's rationale, so no market item sits in an input feed.
